subject: Scaling constraints, scope tradeoffs, and decision path for Greenbank private deploy
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Reed <d.reed@greenbank.com>, it@greenbank.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Greenbank: quick alignment — scope, staffing constraints, and next-decision window

Hi Danielle + Greenbank IT team,

Thanks again for the call this morning. A few follow-ups from our side so we can clarify the deliverable and surface any constraints that would affect schedule or cost:  

Summary of asks from Greenbank (as we heard them):
- VPC + customer-managed transit into Azure East US
- Private deployment with SOC2 + audit-log forwarding to your SIEM
- Data residency enforcement and optional air-gapped patching for sensitive tenants

Open items we need to resolve on Redwood side to give a firm timeline/cost:
1) Production SLA tier and whether you require dedicated reserved GPUs vs. isolated multi-tenant nodes.  
2) Level of integration with your KMS/HSM (bring-your-own-key full wrap vs. token exchange).
3) Ops ownership split: on-call rotations and runbook handoff (we need decision on whether Greenbank ops will take first responder role).

Important constraint: our Dedicated/Private squad has a constrained headcount for Q4. If Greenbank wants dedicated node pools and a 2-week pilot window, we need a firm decision by next Wednesday (2027-09-22) or the earliest GA/pilot starts slip by at least 4–6 weeks due to onboarding queue.

I've attached a short SOW draft and the requirements we captured. Please review and flag anything obviously missing.

Proposed immediate next step: mutual action plan (MAP) with three decision points — Security gating, Procurement terms, and Pilot slot confirmation. If that works, we’ll convert the SOW to a procurement-ready doc and assign owners.

Thanks — Soojin
--
Soojin Lee
Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
Attachment: SOW-draft.docx (1 page stub), greenbank_vpc_requirements.pdf (3 pages)

From: Danielle Reed <d.reed@greenbank.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: it@greenbank.com, procurement@greenbank.com
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 11:18:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Greenbank: quick alignment — scope, staffing constraints, and next-decision window

Soojin — thanks, this is helpful. Couple quick clarifications from our side:  

- We do need dedicated reserved GPUs for predictable latency on the early pilot.
- KMS: we prefer BYOK with HSM-backed key material and proof of key separation in the SOW.
- For ops, Greenbank security wants Redwood to be first responder for the first 30 days post-launch; we’ll take on 2nd-line.

Procurement timeline: procurement team has a 3-week review window once they receive a procurement-ready SOW and contract redlines. I’ve looped procurement in.

Can you confirm whether the SOC2 evidence and audit-log export formats are in the attachments you shared? Danielle

--
Danielle Reed
Head of Platform Security
Greenbank Financial

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Danielle Reed <d.reed@greenbank.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 12:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Greenbank: quick alignment — scope, staffing constraints, and next-decision window

Looping in high-level capacity constraints so expectations are set early:  

- Q4 private onboarding pipeline is 60% booked, our Private rollout team is ~3 FTE short of desired for parallel dedicated pilots.
- If Greenbank requires dedicated node pools + BYOK + extended audit retention (13+ months), we should expect a 25–35% uplift on the initial quote for operational and SRE coverage.

Options to keep timeline:  
- Option A (fastest): Scoped pilot with shared isolated nodes (no tenant-level dedicated GPUs) + full BYOK emulation (Redwood-managed key endpoint that uses customer keys) — pilot in 2–3 weeks, lower cost, later path to dedicated nodes.
- Option B (preferred for performance): Dedicated node pools — requires confirmed budget and procurement sign-off; pilot earliest 6–8 weeks out.

Soojin — can you confirm which option Greenbank is leaning towards? I’ll prepare a staffing plan and delta quote once we have that.

Kimberly
--
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Danielle Reed <d.reed@greenbank.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Greenbank: quick alignment — scope, staffing constraints, and next-decision window

Technical notes from architecture:  
- Dedicated node pools: we need a final decision on model family + token SLAs. For example, serving 13B FLOPS quantized models vs. 70B dense models changes the GPU footprint by ~3–4x.
- Networking: Azure East US peering and transit will need a short firewall ruleset doc from Greenbank (we can prepare template).
- BYOK integration: recommended pattern is to integrate with customer HSM via signed attestation + short-lived session keys. That adds ~5 engineering days to the initial delivery and one security review.

If we go Option A (isolated nodes), we can still run a perf baseline and reserve dedicated pools later with a seamless model migration plan.

Karthik
--
Karthik Iyer
Principal Architect, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Reed <d.reed@greenbank.com>, it@greenbank.com, procurement@greenbank.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Greenbank: quick alignment — scope, staffing constraints, and next-decision window

Thanks all — based on Kimberly and Karthik’s notes, proposing the following MAP to keep momentum without overcommitting our limited Q4 capacity:  

Mutual Action Plan (proposed)
- Decision point 1 (by 2027-09-22): Choose pilot scope — Option A (isolated nodes + BYOK emulation) or Option B (dedicated node pools).
- Decision point 2 (by 2027-09-29): Procurement receives SOW + redlines and confirms 3-week review start date.
- Decision point 3 (by 2027-10-13): Security gating complete (SOC2 evidence + HSM integration plan).

If Greenbank selects Option A by 09/22 we’ll:
- Deliver pilot environment within 2–3 weeks of sign-off.
- Provide an engineering runbook and 30-day Redwood first-response on-call.
- Provide cost delta for later migration to dedicated nodes.

If Greenbank selects Option B we’ll:  
- Queue for dedicated onboarding (6–8 weeks), require procurement sign-off and a 20% commit on reserved capacity for pilot.

Attached: updated SOW draft (procurement-ready skeleton) and a short SOC2 evidence checklist. Please confirm which option you want and whether procurement can begin the SOW review on 09/22.

Thanks — Soojin
--
Attachment: SOW-draft.docx, greenbank_vpc_requirements.pdf
Soojin Lee
Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Danielle Reed <d.reed@greenbank.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, kimberly.park@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@greenbank.com, it@greenbank.com
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 16:12:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Greenbank: quick alignment — scope, staffing constraints, and next-decision window

Soojin / team — we’ll take Option A to keep the pilot timing. Procurement confirms they can start review on 2027-09-22 but will still require the procurement-ready SOW and contract redlines in their queue on that day.

Procurement also flagged a request: please include a section in the SOW that lists the SOC2 report type we will receive (Type II preferred) and the mechanism and frequency for audit-log export (syslog/JSON over TLS). They’ve looped me and will follow up with specific redline comments.

Thanks, Danielle
--
Danielle Reed
Head of Platform Security
Greenbank Financial
